experiment: E17 — Currier A-vs-B contrast (content-controlled, word-class z)
verdict: CONTENT CONFOUND — the E14b A/B word-class difference is a SECTION effect, NOT a dialect difference. B>A holds globally (B−A 1.79) but does NOT survive within the herbal section, where content is held fixed: there herbal-A (1.09) is if anything ABOVE herbal-B (-0.15). So the apparent 'B has more word-class structure' was driven by B covering the biological/recipe sections (which differ from the herbal), not by the Currier dialect. Once content is controlled, there is NO evidence that A and B differ in mid-level word-class structure. This CORRECTS the E14b reading and withdraws the 'A and B are different generative processes' inference from this probe. CAVEAT: Herbal-B is small (3305 tokens), so the within-herbal contrast is UNDERPOWERED — the robust claim is 'the global difference is content-confounded', and the within-content null is suggestive but not decisive; a larger content-matched sample (or a second both-dialect section) would settle it. Word-class z (mean over 6 seeds). GLOBAL A=0.28 B=2.07 (B−A 1.79). HERBAL (content-controlled, 3305 tokens each) A=1.09 B=-0.15 (B−A -1.24; B clearly above A: False). Both strata remain far below real language (z≈15). (L7.)
